events.summary:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

Peace River At Arcadia at SR 70 affecting DeSoto County.

* WHAT...Moderate flooding is occurring and moderate flooding is
forecast.

* WHERE...Peace River at Arcadia at SR 70.

* WHEN...Until late Friday night.

* IMPACTS...At 14.0 feet, Peace River Campground floods and 6 homes
at River Acres are impacted.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 7:30 PM EST Monday the stage was 14.2 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 10.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 7:30 PM EST Monday was 15.0 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to fall below flood stage Friday
evening and continue falling to 9.9 feet Saturday evening.
- Flood stage is 11.0 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 14.2
feet on 06/29/1945.
- https://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

events.summary:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Sanford affecting Seminole County.

.Heavy rainfall has caused river levels on the St. Johns near Sanford
to remain just below Minor flood stage. The river is forecast to
slowly climb into Minor flood stage later this week.

For the St. Johns River...including Sanford...Minor flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Sanford.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 5.5 feet, Water surrounds homes and covers some
driveways in the Stone Island area near Enterprise in Volusia
County. Water enters yards and floods docks in the River Oaks
Estates subdivision.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 7:30 PM EST Monday the stage was 5.4 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 4.2 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise above flood stage at 5.5
feet early Thursday morning. Additional rises are possible
thereafter.
- Flood stage is 5.5 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

events.summary:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Above Lake Harney affecting Seminole County.

.Heavy rainfall has caused river levels on the St. Johns near Geneva
Above Lake Harney to reach Moderate flood stage. A steady rise within
Moderate flood stage is forecast to continue this week. River levels
have the potential to approach Major flood stage next weekend.

For the St. Johns River...Above Lake Harney...Moderate flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Moderate flooding is occurring and forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Above Lake Harney.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 9.3 feet, Many secondary roads are flooded near Lake
Harney. Flooding in the Hatbill Road area near Loughman Lake.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 7:30 PM EST Monday the stage was 9.1 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 6.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 7:30 PM EST Monday was 9.1 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to remain steady above flood
stage at 9.1 to 9.2 feet.
- Flood stage is 8.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

events.summary:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Cocoa 9w affecting Brevard County.

.Recent rainfall over the headwaters of the St. Johns River has
caused Major flooding at the gauge west of Cocoa. Water levels
continue to rise at upstream gauges. The river is forecast to remain
steady near Major flood stage through this week.

For the St. Johns River...including Cocoa 9w...Major flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Major flooding is occurring and forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Cocoa 9w.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 17.2 feet, Water enters homes along the St Johns River
in the Lake Poinsett area west of Cocoa, also low lying homes in
the Silver Pines subdivision in Rockledge and the Shakespeare Park
area of Cocoa. Providence Road area west of Cocoa becomes
impassable, cutting off access to homes in the Mullet Lane and Bass
Road area. Docks flooded and water in parking lot at Lone Cabbage
Fish Camp.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 7:15 PM EST Monday the stage was 17.0 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 15.8 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 7:15 PM EST Monday was 17.0 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to remain steady above flood
stage at 17.0 feet.
- Flood stage is 16.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

St Johns River Near Deland affecting Volusia and Lake Counties.

.Heavy rainfall has caused the St. Johns River near Deland to remain
just below Minor flood stage. The river is forecast to slowly climb
into Minor flood stage later this week.

forecast.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is forecast.

- Bankfull stage is 3.5 feet.

Thursday afternoon and continue rising to 4.0 feet early Thursday
afternoon. Additional rises are possible thereafter.
- Flood stage is 4.0 feet.

events.summary:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Astor affecting Volusia and Lake Counties.

.Heavy rainfall that has occurred upstream has resulted in river
levels just below Moderate flood stage. River levels are expected to
remain steady near Moderate Flood stage through this week and into
the weekend as a large volume of water works north through the basin.

For the St. Johns River...including Astor...Moderate flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Moderate flooding is occurring and forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Astor.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 3.0 feet, Water approaches or may enter lowest homes
on or near Wildhog Road and nearby canals. Flooding reaches the
parking lot of the Juno Trail Apartments. Flooding on portions of
Alligator Road and Holiday Road. Lowest lying yards along Blue
Creek are flooded. Roads at Astor Landing Campground and Lake
Dexter Boat Ramp begin to flood. Water enters lower homes closest
to the river on McPherson Lane.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 7:30 PM EST Monday the stage was 2.9 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 2.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 7:30 PM EST Monday was 2.9 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise slightly to 3 feet late
this week. Additional rises are possible thereafter.
- Flood stage is 2.3 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
